segments.text: XGBoost, SVM, KNN, logistic regression. The interviewer asks: which one would you use, and why?
segments.caption: XGBoost, SVM, KNN, logistic regression. The interviewer asks: which one would you use, and why?

segments.text: Most people guess. After this video, you won't. Save it!
segments.caption: Most people guess. After this video, you won't. Save it!

segments.text: Choosing an algorithm comes down to three questions.
segments.caption: Choosing an algorithm comes down to 3 questions.

segments.text: One: do you have the answers, the labels? Two: are you predicting a number, or a category? Three: is it images, audio or text?
segments.caption: 1: do you have the answers, the labels? 2: are you predicting a number, or a category? 3: is it images, audio or text?

segments.text: Predicting a number? Start with linear regression.
segments.caption: Predicting a number? Start with linear regression.

segments.text: It draws the line that best fits your data. Bigger flat, higher rent.
segments.caption: It draws the line that best fits your data. Bigger flat, higher rent.

segments.text: Need more accuracy on table data? Gradient boosting, like XGBoost.
segments.caption: Need more accuracy on table data? Gradient boosting, like XGBoost.

segments.text: Trees are built one after another, and each new tree fixes the mistakes of the last one. It wins most competitions on table data.
segments.caption: Trees are built one after another, and each new tree fixes the mistakes of the last one. It wins most competitions on table data.

segments.text: Predicting a category, like yes or no? Start with logistic regression.
segments.caption: Predicting a category, like yes or no? Start with logistic regression.

segments.text: It squeezes everything into a probability between zero and one. Will this customer buy? Eighty percent, yes.
segments.caption: It squeezes everything into a probability between 0 and 1. Will this customer buy? 80%, yes.

segments.text: Need to explain every decision? A decision tree.
segments.caption: Need to explain every decision? A decision tree.

segments.text: A flowchart of yes or no questions. Salary above fifty thousand? Any existing loans? Approve, or reject.
segments.caption: A flowchart of yes or no questions. Salary above 50,000? Any existing loans? Approve, or reject.

segments.text: Want a stronger, safer choice? Random forest.
segments.caption: Want a stronger, safer choice? Random forest.

segments.text: Build hundreds of trees, each on a different slice of the data, and let them vote. Banks use it to catch fraud.
segments.caption: Build hundreds of trees, each on a different slice of the data, and let them vote. Banks use it to catch fraud.

segments.text: Classifying text, like spam? Naive Bayes.
segments.caption: Classifying text, like spam? Naive Bayes.

segments.text: It counts how often words appear in spam versus normal mail. Free, winner, urgent? Probably spam.
segments.caption: It counts how often words appear in spam versus normal mail. Free, winner, urgent? Probably spam.

segments.text: Small dataset, two clear classes? A support vector machine.
segments.caption: Small dataset, two clear classes? A support vector machine.

segments.text: It draws the widest possible street between the classes. The points on the edge are the support vectors.
segments.caption: It draws the widest possible street between the classes. The points on the edge are the support vectors.

segments.text: The simplest idea of all? K nearest neighbours.
segments.caption: The simplest idea of all? K nearest neighbours.

segments.text: To label a new point, look at its closest neighbours, and copy the majority.
segments.caption: To label a new point, look at its closest neighbours, and copy the majority.

segments.text: No labels at all, and you want groups? K means clustering.
segments.caption: No labels at all, and you want groups? K means clustering.

segments.text: It drops K centres, gives each point to the nearest one, and moves the centres until the groups settle. Perfect for customer segments.
segments.caption: It drops K centres, gives each point to the nearest one, and moves the centres until the groups settle. Perfect for customer segments.

segments.text: Too many columns? PCA.
segments.caption: Too many columns? PCA.

segments.text: It squeezes a hundred columns into a few that keep most of the information. Faster models, easier plots.
segments.caption: It squeezes 100 columns into a few that keep most of the information. Faster models, easier plots.

segments.text: Images, audio or text at scale? Neural networks.
segments.caption: Images, audio or text at scale? Neural networks.

segments.text: Layers of tiny calculators passing signals forward. Stack enough, and you get deep learning: face unlock, ChatGPT.
segments.caption: Layers of tiny calculators passing signals forward. Stack enough, and you get deep learning: face unlock, ChatGPT.

segments.text: Learning by trial and reward, like a game? Reinforcement learning.
segments.caption: Learning by trial and reward, like a game? Reinforcement learning.

segments.text: An agent tries moves, gets rewards or penalties, and learns the best strategy. That's how AI mastered chess.
segments.caption: An agent tries moves, gets rewards or penalties, and learns the best strategy. That's how AI mastered chess.

scenes.title: What to say in the interview

segments.text: So in the interview, say this. A number? Linear regression, then boosting. A category? Logistic regression, then random forest. Text? Naive Bayes. No labels? K means. Too many columns? PCA. Images? Neural networks.
segments.caption: So in the interview, say this. A number? Linear regression, then boosting. A category? Logistic regression, then random forest. Text? Naive Bayes. No labels? K means. Too many columns? PCA. Images? Neural networks.

segments.text: Save this reel, and send it to a friend preparing for interviews.
segments.caption: Save this reel, and send it to a friend preparing for interviews.
